card.statistical_test_plan: Split segments into duration quartiles; within each quartile, further split into 'stable/transition-free' vs 'contains-transition' subsets using event annotations; compute empirical coverage for each cell; run a 2-way (duration-quartile x transition-content) logistic/GEE regression on interval-containment indicator with subject as random effect; test significance of the duration main effect within the stable-only subset specifically.
card.testable_prediction: Within 'stable, transition-free' segments only, empirical coverage will still show a significant negative correlation with segment duration (Spearman rho<0, p<0.05), indicating a pure noise-aggregation effect independent of event content.

judgment.judge_reason: Testing duration within transition-free segments cleanly separates pure noise accumulation from event content. It controls for event content, recording context and subject. One caveat: the causal path allows either direction ('or vice versa') while the prediction commits to a negative correlation, and averaging over longer windows could reduce noise instead.

card.causal_path: Inter-subject baseline physiology variance -> subject-specific shift/scale of residual (nonconformity score) distribution -> pooled calibration quantile reflects population mixture rather than any individual's true quantile -> mismatch between q_hat and subject-conditional (1-alpha) quantile -> subject-level over/under-coverage
control_variables: Number of segments per subject in calibration set
card.distinguishing_test: Apply subject-stratified (Mondrian) conformal calibration while holding the base model fixed, then compare subject-conditional coverage to nominal.
card.effect_size_rationale: Inter-subject physiological heterogeneity (e.g., resting HR SD across healthy adults ~10-15 bpm) typically produces moderate shifts in residual scale (Cohen's d ~0.3-0.6 in prior personalization studies), enough to move coverage several percentage points off nominal but rarely causing total collapse.
card.failure_condition: No significant correlation (|rho|<0.1, p>0.1) between subject baseline deviation and coverage gap, OR subject-stratified Mondrian recalibration fails to reduce the coverage gap/correlation relative to pooled calibration, indicating base-model fit quality (not quantile pooling) drives the effect.
card.falsification_test: On a leave-subject-out split conformal calibration over >=30 subjects, compute per-subject Mahalanobis distance from calibration-cohort baseline-physiology centroid and correlate with per-subject coverage gap; then apply Mondrian (subject-stratified) conformal calibration with the same base model and retest whether the correlation/coverage gap is eliminated.
card.hypothesis: Coverage instability arises from subject-specific heterogeneity in residual score distributions, so a single global nonconformity score threshold miscalibrates for individuals whose physiology deviates from the calibration cohort's central tendency.
minimum_data_needed: Multi-subject physiological dataset (>=30 subjects) with per-subject baseline physiology metric (resting HR, tonic SCL)
Leave-subject-out calibration/test split with >=20 segments per subject
Base model predictions and true labels per segment
Subject metadata for stratification (age, sex, disease status)
possible_confounders: Disease severity or comorbidity load correlated with baseline physiology
Age/sex differences correlated with both baseline metric and model error
Data collection site/device differences correlated with subject enrollment order
Amount of calibration data per subject (some subjects contribute more segments)
card.proposed_mechanism: Conformal prediction assumes exchangeability of calibration and test residuals; if inter-subject variance in baseline physiology (e.g., resting heart rate, skin conductance baseline) shifts the residual distribution's shape or scale per subject, the empirical quantile computed on pooled calibration data no longer corresponds to the true (1-alpha) quantile for a given held-out subject's segments.
card.rival_explanation: Coverage gaps for atypical subjects are actually caused by base-model underfitting on those subjects (a training-data representation issue), not by pooled-quantile miscalibration.
card.rival_prediction: Subject-conditional coverage gaps will track base-model residual bias measured pre-conformal, and Mondrian/subject-stratified calibration applied post-hoc (with the base model unchanged) will fail to close the gap.
card.statistical_test_plan: Compute per-subject empirical coverage under leave-subject-out split conformal; compute Mahalanobis distance of each subject's baseline metric(s) from calibration cohort centroid; run Spearman/Pearson correlation between distance and coverage-gap (|coverage - (1-alpha)|); use permutation test (1000 shuffles of subject labels) for significance; compare pooled vs Mondrian (subject-stratified) conformal coverage variance via Levene's test.
card.testable_prediction: Per-subject empirical coverage will be negatively correlated with the subject's Mahalanobis distance from the calibration cohort's baseline-physiology centroid (Spearman rho < 0, p<0.05).

judgment.judge_reason: Mondrian calibration by subject gives per-subject coverage whether or not the base model underfits. It would therefore close the gap under both the hypothesis and the rival, so the test cannot separate them. It also needs calibration data from each subject, which conflicts with the leave-subject-out split. Subject heterogeneity is a generic explanation.

card.causal_path: electrode impedance/motion artifact level -> signal noise variance -> nonconformity score magnitude -> deviation from global quantile threshold -> segment-specific miscoverage
control_variables: stratify segments by artifact-free vs artifact-present
use consistent sensor hardware across comparison
card.distinguishing_test: Stratify segments into (clean signal, high label disagreement) vs (noisy signal, low label disagreement) quadrants; compare coverage deviation across quadrants to isolate signal-noise effect from label-noise effect.
card.effect_size_rationale: Motion artifacts in wearable sensors are well-documented to substantially degrade signal quality in a meaningful subset (typically 10-30%) of recording time, producing moderate localized coverage drops.
card.failure_condition: If coverage rates are statistically equal between artifact-flagged and artifact-free segments, hypothesis fails.
card.falsification_test: Apply artifact-adaptive (locally weighted) conformal calibration; if coverage instability across artifact levels is not reduced relative to global calibration, the sensor-noise mechanism is falsified.
card.hypothesis: Sensor-specific noise characteristics that change across recording sessions (e.g., electrode impedance drift, motion artifact rate) cause heteroscedastic nonconformity scores that violate the conformal prediction's assumption of a single exchangeable score distribution.
minimum_data_needed: raw sensor impedance or signal quality metrics
motion artifact annotations
nonconformity scores per segment
independent label quality/agreement metric
possible_confounders: subject_movement_behavior
ambient_temperature_humidity
sensor_model_version
card.proposed_mechanism: Variable electrode-skin contact quality or motion artifacts increase measurement noise variance in some segments, inflating nonconformity scores unevenly; a single global quantile threshold under-covers noisy segments and over-covers clean segments.
card.rival_explanation: Coverage variation is due to underlying label noise (annotation error) rather than sensor signal noise, which happens to correlate with motion because annotators also struggle with noisy segments.
card.rival_prediction: If label noise drives the effect, coverage instability should correlate with annotator disagreement/inter-rater variability even in segments with clean, artifact-free signal.
card.statistical_test_plan: Two-proportion z-test comparing empirical coverage in artifact vs non-artifact strata; logistic regression of miscoverage indicator on artifact severity score.
card.testable_prediction: Segments flagged with high motion artifact or impedance will show significantly lower empirical coverage than artifact-free segments under a fixed global conformal threshold.

judgment.judge_reason: There is a concrete path from electrode impedance and motion artifacts to uneven error variance to under-coverage in noisy segments. The quadrant design (signal noise × label disagreement) separates sensor noise from label noise. The prediction is a directional two-proportion test.

card.causal_path: Segment morphology ambiguity (e.g., transitional sleep stage, borderline QRS) -> elevated inter-rater disagreement/label noise variance -> noisy ground truth inflates or randomizes computed nonconformity score for that segment type -> pooled calibration quantile (averaged across low- and high-noise segment types) miscalibrates for any single segment type -> segment-type-specific coverage deviates from nominal
control_variables: Segment morphology complexity metric independent of label
card.distinguishing_test: Recompute nonconformity scores and coverage using a high-confidence adjudicated subset (segments with near-zero label noise) restricted to structurally similar hard-morphology segments, and compare to the full mixed-agreement set.
card.effect_size_rationale: Magnitude depends on the specific domain's inter-rater agreement distribution (e.g., sleep N1 stage kappa often 0.4-0.5 vs 0.8+ for stable stages), which varies widely across datasets; effect on coverage has not been directly quantified in prior conformal-prediction literature, so a pilot correlation analysis on multi-scorer data is needed to estimate it.
card.failure_condition: Coverage gap persists at similar magnitude on the high-agreement adjudicated hard-segment subset (two-proportion z-test not significant for reduction), indicating intrinsic model difficulty rather than label noise drives the gap; or no significant kappa-coverage correlation is found across segment types.
card.falsification_test: Compute segment-type-level coverage-gap vs (1-kappa) correlation across types, then recompute nonconformity scores and coverage using only a high-agreement adjudicated subset within structurally 'hard' morphology segments to test whether undercoverage persists despite near-zero label noise.
card.hypothesis: Label noise from imperfect ground-truth annotation (e.g., sleep staging by human scorers, arrhythmia labels from imperfect adjudication) varies in rate across signal segment types, differentially inflating nonconformity scores in ways not captured by a single exchangeable calibration distribution.
mechanism_variables: inter-rater label agreement rate (e.g., Cohen's kappa) per segment type
label noise variance by segment/event type
minimum_data_needed: Dataset with multiple independent annotator labels per segment (>=2 scorers) across several segment/event types
Published or computed per-segment-type inter-rater kappa
Base model predictions per segment
Adjudicated/gold-standard label subset for the rival-distinguishing test
possible_confounders: Segment difficulty/ambiguity independently affects both label noise AND true model residual magnitude (e.g., same underlying signal complexity drives both)
Annotator fatigue/experience correlated with which segment types they review
Recording quality (artifact) correlated with ambiguous morphology segments needing more scrutiny
card.proposed_mechanism: Segments with ambiguous morphology (e.g., transitional sleep stages, borderline QRS complexes) have higher inter-rater label disagreement, so the 'true' label used for calibration is itself noisy; this noise is heteroscedastic across segment types, causing the calibration quantile (fit on a mix of low- and high-noise segments) to be miscalibrated for any single segment type.
card.rival_explanation: The coverage gap in ambiguous segments reflects genuine model predictive difficulty on intrinsically hard/complex signal morphology, not noisy ground-truth labels; the model performs worse regardless of label quality.
card.rival_prediction: Coverage undercoverage will persist at similar magnitude even when evaluated against clean, expert-adjudicated labels on the same hard-morphology segments, since the model's residual variance is high independent of label noise.
card.statistical_test_plan: Compute per-segment-type empirical coverage and per-segment-type kappa; run Spearman correlation across segment types (n = number of distinct types, likely small, so use exact permutation test); as the rival-distinguishing test, restrict to a high-agreement adjudicated subset within 'hard' morphology segments and compare coverage to the full mixed-agreement set using a two-proportion z-test.
card.testable_prediction: Segment-type-level coverage-gap magnitude will be positively correlated with (1 - kappa) for that segment type across segment types (Spearman rho>0, p<0.05).

judgment.judge_reason: The mechanism is specific: label-noise rates differ by segment type, tied to kappa (e.g. sleep N1). Using an adjudicated subset of hard-morphology segments separates label noise from intrinsic difficulty. The effect size is stated only as 'unknown', and the correlation across a few segment types has little power.

card.causal_path: Signal morphology atypicality -> annotator/algorithm labeling error rate -> noisy ground truth label -> distorted nonconformity score -> incorrect quantile threshold -> coverage mismatch on morphology-differing test segments
control_variables: use double-annotated subset to estimate label noise per morphology class
stratify analysis by annotator agreement level
card.distinguishing_test: Compare coverage improvement from (a) adding more standard-labeled rare-morphology examples vs (b) relabeling existing rare-morphology examples with a gold-standard adjudicated process at fixed sample size.
card.effect_size_rationale: Label noise magnitude for physiological signals varies widely by dataset and annotation protocol; would need inter-annotator agreement statistics (e.g., Cohen's kappa) per morphology class to estimate effect size.
card.failure_condition: If coverage is uncorrelated with annotator agreement level after controlling for sample size per class, hypothesis fails.
card.falsification_test: Relabel a subset of poorly-covered segments with adjudicated gold-standard labels and recompute coverage; if coverage does not improve despite improved label quality, label-noise mechanism is falsified.
card.hypothesis: Label noise from imperfect ground-truth physiological annotation (e.g., ECG-derived arrhythmia labels) differentially corrupts calibration versus test segments, distorting conformal thresholds.
minimum_data_needed: dataset with dual/gold-standard annotations on a subset
morphology classification metadata
inter-annotator agreement statistics
possible_confounders: disease severity correlating with both atypical morphology and labeling difficulty
annotator fatigue over long recordings
card.proposed_mechanism: Ground truth labels are generated via semi-automated algorithms or human annotators with varying error rates across signal morphologies; segments with atypical morphology have higher label noise, inflating apparent residuals in calibration for those types disproportionately or insufficiently, causing miscalibration when test segment morphology distribution differs.
card.rival_explanation: Coverage differences across morphology classes are due to genuine model underfitting of rare morphology classes (insufficient training examples), not label noise per se.
card.rival_prediction: Coverage will improve for rare morphologies primarily by adding more training/calibration examples with the same (possibly noisy) labeling process, without needing improved label quality.
card.statistical_test_plan: Correlate per-class coverage deviation from nominal against per-class inter-annotator agreement (kappa), using weighted regression accounting for class sample size.
card.testable_prediction: Segments with lower annotator agreement (higher label noise) will show significantly worse conformal coverage than high-agreement segments, holding model performance constant.

judgment.judge_reason: The mechanism is vague ('disproportionately or insufficiently') and depends on an unspecified difference in morphology between calibration and test. 'Holding model performance constant' is not operationalized. Only two confounders are listed, the effect size is unknown and the data needs are loose. The design comparing more examples against relabeling does separate the rival.

card.causal_path: Peripheral perfusion state -> PPG signal quality -> input feature reliability for fused model -> model error magnitude -> mismatch with pooled conformal quantile -> segment coverage deviation by perfusion state
control_variables: stratify analysis by measured perfusion index
include skin tone/contact quality as covariate if available
card.distinguishing_test: Multiple regression of coverage deviation on perfusion index and motion index simultaneously; if perfusion retains significant independent effect, supports modality-reliability mechanism over motion-confound rival.
card.effect_size_rationale: Perfusion-related PPG signal degradation is documented to substantially increase error in pulse-oximetry and HR estimation (published error increases of 20-50% in low-perfusion states), suggesting a moderate-to-large but context-dependent effect.
card.failure_condition: If perfusion index shows no independent association with coverage deviation once motion is controlled for, modality-reliability mechanism is not supported.
card.falsification_test: Implement a perfusion-adaptive conformal scheme (Mondrian conditioning on perfusion index bins); if coverage instability across perfusion strata persists despite this explicit conditioning, mechanism is falsified.
card.hypothesis: Multi-modal sensor fusion models produce unstable coverage across segments because the reliability of one input modality (e.g., PPG) degrades under specific physiological conditions (e.g., low peripheral perfusion) while another modality (e.g., accelerometer) remains reliable, and the fixed conformal quantile does not account for per-segment modality reliability shifts.
minimum_data_needed: perfusion index or proxy (e.g., PPG signal quality index)
synchronized accelerometer motion index
fused multimodal model residuals per segment
segment-level coverage outcomes
possible_confounders: cold ambient temperature simultaneously reducing perfusion and increasing motion (shivering)
skin pigmentation affecting PPG baseline quality independent of perfusion
card.proposed_mechanism: Low peripheral perfusion states reduce PPG signal quality without necessarily being flagged, so the fused model's prediction error increases specifically in low-perfusion segments; since conformal calibration pools all modality-reliability states together, the resulting quantile under-covers low-perfusion segments and over-covers high-perfusion ones.
card.rival_explanation: Coverage deviation attributed to perfusion is actually driven by simultaneous motion artifacts (cold-induced shivering) that independently degrade both modalities, making perfusion a spurious correlate rather than causal driver.
card.rival_prediction: After statistically controlling for motion/accelerometer-derived artifact index, the relationship between perfusion index and coverage deviation disappears.
card.statistical_test_plan: Multiple linear regression or mixed-effects model of coverage deviation on perfusion index and motion index, testing significance of perfusion coefficient.
card.testable_prediction: Segments with low perfusion index will show significantly lower empirical coverage than high-perfusion segments, even after controlling for motion index.

judgment.judge_reason: The mechanism is specific: low perfusion degrades PPG while the accelerometer stays reliable. Controlling for motion index separates it from the shivering confound. However, Mondrian binning by perfusion guarantees coverage within each bin by construction, so the falsification test is nearly tautological. The regression-based failure condition is still valid.
